Anyone grow figs? I have some questions.
Figs eat wasps. That's all you need to know about figs. That they're fucking wasp corpse containers. When you eat figs you're eating fucking dead wasps.
Figs are delicious, wasps and all. Just came into say that

Pruning fig trees is a nightmare if you do not know the history of when it last gave fruit. A fig tree that doesnt go ripe usually means that it is producing more fruit than it can handle. Or, it is one of those wasp figs that need wasp corpses to grow. Where I am in Australia we do not get the wasp figs, so whatever.

You will need to cut the tree back, but you can not cut it too much back or it will put more energy into growing branches than leaf/fruit shoots. If you do not cut it back enough, your fruit may grow bigger or get one step closer to ripening, but still not ripen.

Fruit is generally good with the bottom is splitting open like an alien egg or when very soft. Birds will eat the fruit before it goes ripe, you will need a net. Figs do not ripen further after you pick them, but they will go softer, which generally makes them more edible but they will still taste a bit weird.

If you have low lying branches with fruit and a net, animals will destroy your net to get to the fruit. Im at the point now where Im going to trap and eat every damn possum I can find because of the damage they sometimes do to my stuff.
So will I need to start trimming this bush back in order to make it grow vertical or can I just leave it a bush?

You can, but I do not recommend it if you want to the most fruit out of it and more so if you have animals nearby that will go for it. It can be useful if you want to propagate it as low branches sitting on the ground can take root, then you can just cut it off from the main tree and hey, new fig tree. Do keep in mind though that there are many different fig trees that grow in different ways. They are ones that grow as vines and ones that dont fruit.
